# ADR-005 — Published terms and simulated payment

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Applies to** US-03  
**Basis** [Approved US-03 Draft 2](../../spec/US-03.md), [specification approval](../approvals/US-03-spec-approval.md), assessment pp. 2 and 8–9

## Context

[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves a country-scoped terms document and public read action. [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern. [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps quote state and payment in the browser, and [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) already gates editable Summary on valid Details and a freshly revalidated plan. The existing Angular 21.2 wizard has the Summary handoff and the Strapi 5.63 controller already serves Form and Plans through the same-origin proxy. US-03 needs a terms revision contract, a payment attempt that refreshes consent before it starts, and a terminal receipt that survives reload.

## Proposed decision

### Published terms contract

Create a Terms collection with Draft & Publish and one document per country. Use the existing country enum and a required, nonblank multiline plain-text body of at most 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Preserve the body as returned by Strapi, including paragraph breaks. Read only the published country document through the Document Service, selecting only country and body. Read up to two documents to detect duplicate publications and fail if either the country or body is invalid. Seed one fictitious, country-specific publication for Colombia and Chile in the existing startup workflow. Track seeding separately from Forms and Plans, skip countries with existing Terms documents during initial seeding, and preserve editorial changes and deliberate unpublication on subsequent starts. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)

Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Valid published document | `200` with the terms envelope |
| Unexpected query parameters or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
| No published document | `404 TERMS_NOT_PUBLISHED` |
| Duplicate or invalid published configuration | `503 TERMS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| CMS retrieval failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |

Reuse the `{ error: { code } }` envelope and `Cache-Control: no-store` on handler outcomes. Extend the same-origin, GET-only proxy allowlist and add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readTerms` to the Public role alongside Form and Plans. Generated CRUD, draft and admin access, and write credentials stay outside the public contract. The terms request carries the country in the path and no quote, consent or payment data. The proxy bypasses caching as it does for Form and Plans. [HTTP caching](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)

### Summary and consent

Extend the existing Summary handoff. Build a read-only review projection from the active country's validated, reconciled Details and freshly selected Plan. Use current field order, labels and option labels, the existing money formatter and the plan's final price. Mask the `identityDocument` value before it enters the review projection so both visible and accessible output use the same masked string. Apply Q-US03-01 to alphanumeric characters, preserving separators. Keep the raw value in the existing Details draft only. There is no additional form field or network contract for the review.

Read Terms on Summary entry and explicit retry through the existing `HttpClient` and signals pattern. Bind consent in memory to the active country, terms revision and the review snapshot. Compare snapshots by value using the current field identifiers, kinds and normalized values, and the selected plan ID and final money value. Navigation back to edit preserves Details and the plan candidate under their existing rules. A change to normalized quote data, plan, price or terms revision invalidates consent. Cancellation and generation checks prevent superseded responses from replacing active terms. Loading or failed terms reads leave the review available and prevent payment. [Angular HTTP requests](https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests)

### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery

1. The quote feature owns one attempt state per country. A single Pay command checks the live editable Summary prerequisites, consent and absence of a busy or completed payment. It synchronously reserves an attempt before requesting fresh country Terms. That reservation locks submission during both the refresh and the simulation. The attempt captures the country, active Summary generation, consent binding and the selected demo outcome.
2. Only the current attempt may act on the refresh result. Recheck the active country and Summary generation, current Details and plan validity, quote snapshot, and consent. A valid changed revision replaces the presented terms and clears consent. A failed or invalid read leaves a recoverable terms error. Both outcomes release the reservation without invoking the simulator. A matching revision advances directly to processing under the same reservation.
3. The local asynchronous simulator accepts only the captured Approved or Rejected outcome. Approved is the selector default. Outcome changes after reservation apply to a subsequent attempt. The simulator has no external side effects and takes no card, Details or plan data. Only the matching live attempt may settle. Rejection releases the lock with a retryable error and keeps the draft, selected plan and matching consent. A retry goes through the same Pay command and a fresh terms read. Leaving Summary, switching country or replacing the quote invalidates outstanding work. Cancel pending reads and ignore callbacks that can no longer settle. Browser Back or Forward cannot replay Pay.
4. Success creates one browser-generated opaque simulated quote number and commits an immutable terminal receipt once. Persist only the minimal completed receipt in a bounded, versioned country-scoped `sessionStorage` record alongside the existing draft and plan entries. Keep country and quote number in the receipt. Decode the record as untrusted input, rejecting oversized, unknown-version, malformed or wrong-country values. Consent and unfinished attempts stay in memory. After reload, an interrupted attempt therefore cannot resume or settle. The person returns through the existing Details and plan checks and can retry after current consent. If storage is unavailable, retain the same duplicate guard and receipt for the current page session under ADR-003. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
5. A valid restored receipt is the terminal confirmation for the current country quote. On the Summary route, restore that confirmation without opening editable Summary or presenting live plan, price or terms as part of the receipt. CMS changes do not alter a settled result. History traversal and switching back to that country preserve the receipt and cannot make the same quote payable. Only an explicit start-new-quote reset under ADR-003 may clear that country's receipt, draft, plan and in-memory payment state. Clear the terminal lock last so a partial reset cannot silently reopen the completed quote. Editable Summary for an unfinished or explicitly reset quote still uses the live prerequisite redirects in ADR-004.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Embed Terms in Form Configuration or expose generated Strapi reads | Embedding ties independent publication schedules together. Generated reads widen the public surface. The dedicated action adds one bounded response and Public permission. |
| Use `updatedAt`, `publishedAt` or an editor-entered revision | Metadata can change while the displayed text is unchanged. Manual revisions can drift from text. The content fingerprint follows what the person reviews and accepts. |
| Trust terms from Summary entry or lock only once simulation begins | Entry-only terms can miss a published change. A later lock allows overlapping Pay refreshes. Reserving before the fresh read costs one terms request per eligible Pay attempt and closes that overlap. A CMS publication after the successful read may still occur while the local simulation runs. |
| Persist consent and unfinished attempts or require fresh CMS data to restore a receipt | Persisting in-flight state needs restoration rules and risks replay. Revalidating a historical receipt against current editorial data can erase access to a completed result. A minimal terminal record supports reload without reviving unfinished work or copying quote details. |
| Add a server-side payment endpoint | Server persistence could coordinate across tabs or devices. The approved simulator is local, so tab-scoped duplicate protection has no server or gateway dependency. |

## Verification

- Use AC-US03-01, AC-US03-02 and AC-US03-04 / T-US03-01, T-US03-02 and T-US03-04 to verify the review projection and same-country edit path in Colombia and Chile. Check that the full document is absent from the visible and accessible Summary.
- Use AC-US03-03 and AC-US03-09 / T-US03-03 and T-US03-11 to verify country-isolated published reads, revision changes and identical republishes, draft isolation, missing/invalid/unavailable terms, fresh Pay reads and consent invalidation. Verify the Public role and proxy allow only the intended content reads, and confirm a published terms edit reaches the running Angular build.
- Use AC-US03-05 through AC-US03-08 and AC-US03-10 / T-US03-05 through T-US03-09 to verify one attempt through both phases, deterministic Approved and Rejected in both countries, retry, late responses after navigation, and reload of interrupted and completed states. Check wrong-country and corrupt storage, memory fallback, and completed receipt recovery after rejected live prerequisites without opening editable Summary. T-US03-10 covers the full flow at project verification.

| Pattern | Design contract |
| --- | --- |
| Header and country selection | The global header shows product identity. The picker and recovery for unsupported routes offer links to supported countries. The URL sets the active country and its isolated quote state. Include a main landmark, skip link and unique heading. On wizard navigation, focus the new screen heading. |
| Progress track | An informational ordered list of Datos, Plan and Resumen, centered on desktop. Mark the current step with `aria-current="step"` and expose completed status as text to assistive technology. Use separate Back and Edit actions. |

| Field feedback | Neutral on initial render. Show the configured error on invalid blur or unsuccessful Continue. Update or clear it as touched values change. Set `aria-invalid` while showing the error and move focus to the first invalid field on Continue. |

**Status** Proposed · Pending human design approval

**Basis** [Approved US-03](../../spec/US-03.md), [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md) and [US-02 plan selection](US-02-plan-selection.md).

## Wireframes

| View | Review frames |
| --- | --- |
| Editable Summary | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-summary-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-summary-mobile.svg) |
| Terms and payment states | [In-place variants on the compact lane](wireframes/US-03-terms-and-payment-states.svg) |
| Confirmation, including reload | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-mobile.svg) |

Each country uses the same layouts and control order. The examples use fictitious values, local currency formatting and sample terms. The app presents the active country's published terms and current field and plan labels.

## Editable Summary

- Reuse the app header, main landmark, route-entry heading focus and informational **Datos / Plan / Resumen** stepper. A review heading identifies the step. The selected country is visible in the terms heading and the plan's currency.
- Show **Titular y vehículo** as a definition list in configured order with a nearby **Editar datos** link to same-country Details. Use the projected masked document in visible and accessible text. The **Plan elegido** card shows the current plan and final price with **Cambiar plan** linking to same-country Plans. Use the approved formatter with explicit **COP** or **CLP**. Both links preserve state under the existing Details and Plans rules.
- Put **Términos y condiciones de {país}** next in reading order. Present the plain text inline with preserved paragraph breaks. The page scrolls as the text grows. The labeled, initially unchecked native consent checkbox follows the text. Its checked state reflects consent for the current quote and revision. Show **Acepta los términos para continuar.** beside the unavailable payment action while acceptance is outstanding.
- Use a native radio group with visible legend **Resultado del pago (solo demostración)** and the options **Aprobado** and **Rechazado**. Default to **Aprobado** on initial entry. Associate **No se realizará un cobro real.** with the group as help. **Simular pago** is the single Pay action for either outcome and every payment retry. Its eligibility follows ADR-005.
- At 64 rem and above, use the established centered 58 rem composition with Details and plan side by side, followed by a reading lane for terms, consent, outcome and Pay. Below 64 rem, stack the plan after Details using the same DOM order. At compact widths, retain 16–20 px side gutters and use a full-width Pay button. Use auto-height panels, wrapping labels and unbroken-value wrapping where needed. Keep the action in normal page flow.

Reuse the existing `app-wizard-progress` and status-panel pattern, Tailwind canvas/paper/context/ink/line tokens, existing input and focus utilities, and the approved success, error and disabled treatments. Section titles, price emphasis and the quote number follow the approved type scale. Keep 44 px link and control targets and the 48 px primary action. [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md), [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Terms and payment states

| State | Visible response and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Reading terms on entry or retry | Keep the review and price visible. In the terms region show **Cargando términos…** until usable content is ready. Consent is unavailable and Pay stays disabled. |
| Terms unavailable | For empty, invalid or failed reads, including the Pay refresh, show **No pudimos cargar los términos.** with **Reintentar carga** in the terms region. Keep Details and plan. Pay stays blocked. If a successful recovery returns the same terms revision, text and quote snapshot, previously accepted consent can remain checked. Recovery returns to the review without starting payment. |
| Checking terms on Pay | Keep the review visible and reserve the single Pay action. Show **Comprobando los términos…** and disable repeat activation. The simulator begins only after the fresh read confirms the accepted terms and quote. |
| Terms changed on Pay | Replace the terms with the new text, clear consent, and show **Los términos cambiaron. Léelos y acéptalos para continuar.** before the updated text. A new acceptance followed by another **Simular pago** is required. |
| Processing | Keep the review, plan, terms and consent visible. Show **Procesando el pago simulado…** and keep Pay locked until settlement. An interrupted reload returns to the editable review if its prerequisites pass. Fresh consent is required before retry. |
| Rejected | Show **Pago simulado rechazado.** by the payment controls with **Tu cotización se conservó. Elige un resultado y vuelve a simular el pago.** The chosen **Rechazado** option remains visible. The user can select **Aprobado** or retry the chosen outcome using the same action. Retain Details, plan and still-current consent. |
| Approved | Replace all editable content with a terminal receipt. Show **Pago simulado aprobado**, **No se realizó un cobro.**, the country and a selectable **Número de cotización**. Keep the existing product header and completed stepper. On reload or return to the same completed quote, show the same reference even if published content changed. |
| Details or plan prerequisite missing | Reuse the existing redirect and recovery patterns for the earliest incomplete same-country step. Editable Summary is available after successful revalidation. |

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Use contextual anchor text for edits, an associated native checkbox label, and a native `fieldset` and `legend` for the radios. Keyboard order follows the review, terms, checkbox, radio group and Pay. Use standard Tab, Space, Enter and arrow-key behavior. Keep the disabled reason or status visible beside Pay. Preserve visible focus and the native outline in forced colors. [WAI grouping controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
- Announce loading, fresh checks and processing through a stable polite status region. Announce actionable failures once, using the existing accessible feedback pattern. Keep focus where it is while async work runs, with the focused Pay control retained as a target during the busy state. Convey the disabled state programmatically and suppress both keyboard and pointer activation while it remains focusable. If changed terms interrupt an active Pay interaction, move focus to the updated terms heading so it precedes the new text and checkbox. On terms failure, use the recovery control as the focus destination if the initiating target disappeared or became unavailable. A failed recovery with a stable Retry control keeps focus there. A successful recovery that removes the Retry control returns focus to the terms heading. A user who moved to an edit link while waiting keeps their focus.
- On rejection, announce the result while keeping focus in place if its target is still present. The user can reach the outcome choices from Pay with Shift+Tab. On first confirmation or a restored receipt, focus its heading and expose the reference as nearby selectable text. The heading and receipt content communicate success without relying on icon or color. Use a static busy cue under reduced motion. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design verification map

| Approved criteria | Checks for implementation and QA |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-01, 02, 04 and 08 | Check both country projections, masked visible and spoken document values, option labels, currency, edit links and prerequisite recovery. |
| AC-US03-03 and 09 | Check long published terms at narrow widths, missing/invalid content, fresh Pay checks, a changed revision with renewed acceptance, and terms retry with focus and draft retention. |
| AC-US03-05, 06 and 07 | Exercise both outcome choices in each country, locked activation through both busy phases, rejection-to-approval retry, interrupted reload and same-number terminal receipt restoration. |
| AC-US03-10 | Check keyboard order, visible and unobscured focus, announcements, target sizes, reduced motion, forced colors and reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. |

The wireframes and interaction guidance are pending human design approval.
"}

# Modern Web Guidance

Search and retrieve standardized modern web best practices at the **start** of implementing or updating any web UI, CSS layout/animation, or client-side JS logic (dates/timezones, sanitization, performance, accessibility, UX fixes) before writing ad-hoc solutions or adding dependencies.

## Primary Workflow

### Step 1. Search Use Cases

Run `modern-web-guidance` directly with `npx` using a **2–5 word action-oriented English query** for a **single web platform capability or UI pattern**:
- **Keep queries focused and generic**: Describe the user-visible capability (`<verb> + <UI/platform object>`, optionally paired with the target HTML/CSS/JS feature name if known). Omit framework/library names (`React`, `Vue`, `Tailwind`, etc.) and app/domain nouns (product, route, or component/file names). Split multi-feature tasks into separate `search` calls.
- **Name implied UI primitives**: When the user's prompt expresses intent without naming the UI primitive (e.g. "confirm first", "delete with confirmation", "pick a date"), translate the domain intent into the implied UI component or platform mechanism (e.g. search `"confirmation modal dialog"` or `"confirm dialog"` rather than `"confirm destructive action"`, or `"date picker input"` rather than `"pick a date"`).
- **Example**: Search `"light dismiss dialog"` or `"responsive data table"`, **not** `"dialog"` (too terse), `"responsive table dark mode"` (compound — split into two searches), or `"close React settings modal on outside click"` (framework/app noise).

```sh
npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest search "<query>" --skill-version 2026_11_10-47b4c80e
```

> **Note**: Returns `[{ "id", "description" }, ...]`. Judge results by their `description` fields:
> - **Match found**: Call `retrieve` directly—do not also run `list`.
> - **Weak or empty results**: If `search` returns `[]` or unrelated descriptions, **rephrase `search` once** using the concrete HTML/CSS/UI component noun or synonym (e.g., `dialog`, `modal`, `popover`, `table`, `form`) before falling back to `list` (or use `list` once for broad UI audits).
> - **Topic not covered**: If no `description` matches after rephrasing, proceed without retrieving unrelated guides.

### Step 2. Retrieve Best Practices

Once you have relevant `id`(s) from the search results, call `retrieve` to get the full guide(s)—including both specific use-case guides that match your task and any broader discipline guide (e.g., `html`, `css`, `forms`, `accessibility`, `color`, `performance`, `security`) that applies. You can pass multiple IDs separated by commas.

```sh
npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "<id>"
```

If `retrieve` saves large output (> 9.5 KB) to a temporary file to prevent truncation, read that file path in full using your file-reading tool (reading remaining line ranges if needed)—do not use `cat` or `head`.

### Step 3. Verify Guidance Compliance

When generating or modifying code, cross-check the implementation against the retrieved guide before concluding:
- **Applicable Guidance & Fallbacks**: Ensure the relevant modern patterns and necessary fallback strategies from the guide are correctly applied, without forcing unrequested features.
- **Task Fulfillment**: Confirm that the implementation fully satisfies the user's request.
- Do not run `legacy-scan`; it's for detecting legacy patterns to modernize, not this.

### Step 4. Disclose Skill Usage

When you consult `modern-web-guidance` for a task, end the response where you deliver those changes with a `### Modern Web Guidance` section:
- **When retrieved guides shaped your code**: Write **one** bullet (1–2 sentences, ≤75 words) per newly applied `<id>` in first-person voice explaining the non-obvious implementation choices, CSS/API overrides, or fallbacks `<id>` required and the pitfall it prevented, anchored by a short verbatim quote of that specific rule or gotcha (never the guide's intro overview):

  - **Never** guess `<id>`s or quotes from memory after context compaction (re-run `search`/`retrieve` if needed), and credit **only** guide-backed changes from the current turn.
- **When searched/listed in this turn but zero guides applied**: Write one first-person sentence naming which topics or guides you checked in `modern-web-guidance` and why none applied (omit if any guide applied).

# Test-Driven Development

## Overview

Write a failing test before writing the code that makes it pass. For bug fixes, reproduce the bug with a test before attempting a fix. Tests are proof — "seems right" is not done. A codebase with good tests is an AI agent's superpower; a codebase without tests is a liability.

## When to Use

- Implementing any new logic or behavior
- Fixing any bug (the Prove-It Pattern)
- Modifying existing functionality
- Adding edge case handling
- Any change that could break existing behavior

**When NOT to use:** Pure configuration changes, documentation updates, or static content changes that have no behavioral impact.

**Related:** For browser-based changes, combine TDD with runtime verification using Chrome DevTools MCP — see the Browser Testing section below.

## Discover the Stack First

The TDD cycle is universal; the commands are not. Before writing the first test, discover how *this* repository tests, and use its commands for every RED, GREEN, and verification step:

- **Language and build system** — `package.json`, `pom.xml`/`build.gradle`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `Gemfile`, a `Makefile`
- **Checked-in wrappers** — prefer `./gradlew`, `./mvnw`, `make test`, or a repo script over globally installed tools
- **Test framework and configuration** — and how it runs a single focused test vs the full suite
- **Existing conventions** — where tests live, how files are named, what patterns neighboring tests follow
- **Documented commands** — README, CONTRIBUTING, and CI workflows show the commands that actually gate merges

Run the repository's focused-test command during the loop and its full-suite command before completion. Never assume a default like `npm test` — a Gradle, Cargo, or pytest project has its own equivalent.

```

 Write a test    Write minimal code    Clean up the

# Multi-Country Car Insurance — Technical Assessment

One Angular 21 application serves the Colombia and Chile quote wizard. Strapi 5 publishes each country's form configuration and plan catalog. The wizard covers details entry, plan selection, and the handoff to Summary. Quote and vehicle values use fictitious data and stay in the browser.

## Run the wizard

Use Docker with Compose and run the following command from the repository root.

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

Open [the country picker](http://localhost:8080). Both [Colombia](http://localhost:8080/co/quote/details) and [Chile](http://localhost:8080/cl/quote/details) support direct links. The first startup builds the app and publishes sample forms and plans for both countries into a Strapi SQLite volume. It generates Strapi secrets in that local volume. Restarts preserve later editorial changes.

The public wizard and the seeded forms and plans are available as soon as the stack is ready. An administrator account is optional for evaluating the wizard. To edit content, open [Strapi's loopback administration panel](http://localhost:1337/admin) and create the first local administrator using the registration form shown on a fresh volume. This is the local Strapi account and requires no Strapi Cloud account. Administrator credentials stay with the local Strapi instance. See the [Strapi first-run guide](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/quick-start).

In Content Manager, open **Quote form configuration**, edit fields within the existing form for the selected country, then publish the complete form. Reload the application or open the other country URL to fetch current content. Ordinary navigation within the same country's wizard reuses the ready configuration in memory.

In Content Manager, open **Quote plan** to edit a country's plans. Publish each plan and set it active to offer it. Enter base prices in major units with currency COP for Colombia (up to two fractional digits) or CLP for Chile (whole pesos). The published base price is the final price. Plans are read on entry to the plan step and checked again at the Summary handoff. The user must choose again if their plan was removed or repriced.

### Synchronize an existing local sample plan catalog

New databases already receive all three plans for each country. For the default local Compose volume created with the original two-plan catalog, build the current CMS image and preview the changes.

```sh
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance build cms
sh scripts/sync-dev-plans.sh --dry-run
```

The preview reads a consistent SQLite backup with the development volume mounted read-only. Review the proposed changes and copy the reported fingerprint when the status is `ready`. If the status is `blocked`, review the listed records in Strapi. A `noop` means the catalog is current.

```sh
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance stop web cms
sh scripts/sync-dev-plans.sh --apply FINGERPRINT
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance up -d
```

Replace `FINGERPRINT` with the value from the preview. Apply requires the stopped development volume and saves a database backup in that volume before writing. It recomputes the preview and checks both the draft and published versions in one transaction. Only exact original fixtures receive expanded benefits, and they retain their document IDs. The sync introduces Integral only when both country catalogs match the original fixtures and both Integral documents are absent. Conflicting edits, duplicates, unexpected or missing versions, and prior removal of a tracked Integral stop the whole update. The local administrator account and other content stay in the original volume.

If the owner approves preserving an existing Colombia Ruta price, add `--preserve-co-ruta-price PRICE` to both preview and apply. Use COP major units with two decimal places and no grouping separators. For example, use `--preserve-co-ruta-price 179900.00` for COP 179.900,00. Both stored versions must already have exactly that price. The sync preserves it and still checks every other field against the fixtures.

## Configuration and data boundaries

- The public app uses same-origin GET paths under `/api/quote-content/v1/:country/` for `form`, `plans`, and `terms`. The Strapi Public role has only `readForm`, `readPlans`, and `readTerms` under `api::quote-content.quote-content`. The static host proxies these three reads. The public frontend uses no API token.
- Never add duplicate field keys, option keys or semantic purposes. Field order is numeric, then stable field key on ties. Date of birth with the 18-year rule and vehicle year with its range rule are required for a usable form.
- Enter a rule argument or field default in the Strapi JSON editor as an object with a single `value` property, for example `{"value": 18}`, `{"value": false}` or `{"value": "2020-01-01"}`. Leave it empty for argument-free rules or fields with no default. Required selects start unselected and cannot have defaults. Present but invalid content leaves the whole form unavailable with a retry action.
- The version 1 decoder accepts up to 40 fields, 60 options per select, 12 rules per field and 240 UTF-16 units per content string. Text values allow up to 256 Unicode code points. Patterns are whole-value checks limited to 120 pattern units, literal characters, character classes and bounded counts through 24. The matcher uses a bounded set of offsets.
- Each country catalog may include up to 40 active published plans with up to 20 entries per coverage or benefit list. Plans sort by numeric order, then stable document ID. A malformed active published plan makes the country's catalog unavailable until the content is corrected.
- Drafts and plan choices are isolated by URL country and retained in the current tab's `sessionStorage`, with a memory fallback if storage is unavailable. Reload revalidates against fresh published configuration. Quote data is excluded from API payloads, shareable URLs, and server persistence. SQLite holds Strapi content and its administrative metadata.

# Multi-Country Car Insurance — Technical Assessment

One Angular 21 application serves the Colombia and Chile quote wizard. Strapi 5 publishes each country's form configuration and plan catalog. The wizard covers details entry, plan selection, and the handoff to Summary. Quote and vehicle values use fictitious data and stay in the browser.

## Run the wizard

Use Docker with Compose and run the following command from the repository root.

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

Open [the country picker](http://localhost:8080). Both [Colombia](http://localhost:8080/co/quote/details) and [Chile](http://localhost:8080/cl/quote/details) support direct links. The first startup builds the app and publishes sample forms and plans for both countries into a Strapi SQLite volume. It generates Strapi secrets in that local volume. Restarts preserve later editorial changes.

The public wizard and the seeded forms and plans are available as soon as the stack is ready. An administrator account is optional for evaluating the wizard. To edit content, open [Strapi's loopback administration panel](http://localhost:1337/admin) and create the first local administrator using the registration form shown on a fresh volume. This is the local Strapi account and requires no Strapi Cloud account. Administrator credentials stay with the local Strapi instance. See the [Strapi first-run guide](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/quick-start).

In Content Manager, open **Quote form configuration**, edit fields within the existing form for the selected country, then publish the complete form. Reload the application or open the other country URL to fetch current content. Ordinary navigation within the same country's wizard reuses the ready configuration in memory.

In Content Manager, open **Quote plan** to edit a country's plans. Publish each plan and set it active to offer it. Enter base prices in major units with currency COP for Colombia (up to two fractional digits) or CLP for Chile (whole pesos). The published base price is the final price. Plans are read on entry to the plan step and checked again at the Summary handoff. The user must choose again if their plan was removed or repriced.

### Synchronize an existing local sample plan catalog

New databases already receive all three plans for each country. For the default local Compose volume created with the original two-plan catalog, build the current CMS image and preview the changes.

```sh
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance build cms
sh scripts/sync-dev-plans.sh --dry-run
```

The preview reads a consistent SQLite backup with the development volume mounted read-only. Review the proposed changes and copy the reported fingerprint when the status is `ready`. If the status is `blocked`, review the listed records in Strapi. A `noop` means the catalog is current.

```sh
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance stop web cms
sh scripts/sync-dev-plans.sh --apply FINGERPRINT
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance up -d

It recomputes the preview and checks both the draft and published versions in one transaction. Only exact original fixtures receive expanded benefits, and they retain their document IDs. The sync introduces Integral only when both country catalogs match the original fixtures and both Integral documents are absent. Conflicting edits, duplicates, unexpected or missing versions, and prior removal of a tracked Integral stop the whole update. text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:`ls frontend/public/icons; python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('README.md')
s=p.read_text().replace("Strapi 5 publishes each country's form configuration and plan catalog. The wizard covers details entry, plan selection, and the handoff to Summary.", "Strapi 5 publishes each country's form configuration, plan catalog, and terms. The wizard covers details entry, plan selection, quote review, consent, and simulated payment.").replace("publishes sample forms and plans", "publishes sample forms, plans, and terms").replace("seeded forms and plans", "seeded forms, plans, and terms")
anchor="### Synchronize an existing local sample plan catalog"
s=s.replace(anchor, """In Content Manager, open **Quote terms** and edit the existing Terms document for the country. Publish the document to make its multiline plain text available on Summary. Terms are checked again on Pay. If the published text has changed, the user must review and accept the updated terms before paying.

The demo-only outcome defaults to Approved. Select Rejected to test recovery, then select Approved and retry with the same quote. A successful simulation shows a quote number that survives reload in the same tab when browser storage is available.

"""+anchor)
s=s.replace("- Drafts and plan choices are isolated by URL country", "- Each country has one published Terms document with a nonblank body of up to 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Missing, duplicate or invalid published terms block payment until recovered.\\n- Drafts and plan choices are isolated by URL country")
s=s.replace("and [US-02 specification](spec/US-02.md) define", ", [US-02 specification](spec/US-02.md), and [US-03 specification](spec/US-03.md) define").replace("](spec/US-01.md) ,", "](spec/US-01.md),")
s=s.replace("- [Workflow](FLOW.md)", "- [ADR-005](docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md) and the [US-03 design](docs/design/US-03-summary-and-payment.md) cover terms, consent, and simulated payment.\\n- [Workflow](FLOW.md)")
s=s.replace("US-03 quote summary, country terms, and simulated payment are pending. Project-level end-to-end verification through payment depends on US-03. Native screen-reader verification remains pending because the US-02 browser runs did not include a native assistive-technology session.", "Independent US-03 verification and final human approval are pending. Native screen-reader verification remains pending.")
p.write_text(s)
p=Path('frontend/src/styles.css')
s=p.read_text().replace('#1d603d','#1f5b39').replace('#e8f5eb','#e8f5ec')
p.write_text(s)
PY

docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:15:### Gate the wizard on the terminal receipt
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:17:Keep `/:country/quote/summary` as the confirmation route for a completed quote. Continue using the existing route parameter subscription, including for a reused quote component and browser history. Decode the country and synchronously resolve its terminal receipt before exposing any editable route state or requesting live quote content. A valid receipt takes precedence over Details, Plans and editable Summary. Replace an attempted same-country Details or Plans history entry with the canonical Summary URL and render only confirmation. No editable control is instantiated while the redirect is pending. Confirmation reads the receipt directly and has no form, catalog or terms prerequisite. Keep the terminal check reactive so successful completion also switches the current Summary to confirmation without waiting for a navigation. [Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state) · [Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:19:Reuse the route and attempt generations to suppress superseded work at navigation and restart. A retained event or delayed response must not re-enter an editable step, persist an old draft or plan, or settle an attempt after the quote becomes terminal or its state is reset. Receipt lookup and redirect decisions always use the canonical active country. Rejection creates no receipt and keeps the existing edit, plan selection and retry behavior, including a fresh terms check on Pay.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:23:After the live attempt passes its final eligibility check, use the existing review projector to capture ordered label and display-value rows, including the already masked identity document. Capture the chosen plan's displayed name and validated final `{ amountMinor, currency }` at the same transition. Generate the existing opaque quote reference once and commit the immutable receipt as one snapshot. Copy display values out of the editable state. Restore and display the snapshot with the existing country money formatter. A published change, removal or outage cannot alter it. Treat values as plain text in both visible and accessible output.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:25:Store `{ version: 2, country, number, review: { rows, planName, price } }` in the existing per-country receipt key, `quote-receipt-v1:<country>`. The key stays stable. The envelope version determines the decoder. Persist only row id, display label and display value for each row, alongside the plan name and typed price. Keep the raw document, full draft, full plan catalog, terms, consent and attempt data out of the receipt.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:27:Validate one bounded envelope before rendering. Check version, country, quote reference format, ordered rows with unique valid field ids, text limits and country money. Use the existing form and plan contract limits as the source for bounds. The current contract permits 40 rows, field ids of up to 40 safe characters, labels and plan names of up to 240 UTF-16 code units, and free text of up to 256 Unicode code points. A projected value therefore needs up to 512 UTF-16 code units, including supplementary characters. The field and string limits plus worst-case JSON escaping, price and envelope fit within a 200,000 UTF-16 code unit pre-parse limit. Use only the decoded fields for rendering. An invalid version 2 record does not fall back to a reference-only receipt. If writing a valid receipt fails, preserve the full terminal receipt and duplicate lock in memory under ADR-003 and surface that reload recovery is unavailable. Never write a partial or version 1 substitute.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:29:Continue decoding the existing version 1 envelope in that same key with its original bounds and country and number checks. It restores the original reference, terminal gate and restart behavior. Its historical review is unavailable. There is no backfill from mutable state and no migration write during restore. The single key avoids a second legacy lookup that could revive an old receipt after restart.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:31:### Restart and release the terminal lock last
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:33:Use one restart command for the active country and terminal receipt. Run the synchronous persistence sequence through the existing state owners, with an explicit outcome for every storage action. The current draft and candidate persistence helpers can swallow failures for ordinary edits. Restart must observe failures and may not use silent success from those paths. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:35:1. Keep confirmation and the terminal guard in place throughout reset. Invalidate pending country-scoped form, plan, terms and payment work before clearing persisted state. Ignore repeated reset requests while a reset is in progress.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:36:2. Remove the active country's draft and candidate keys and read each back to confirm absence. A failure stops the reset before touching the receipt key. A partially cleared draft or candidate stays inaccessible behind the receipt. Retry repeats the removals safely. The other country is outside this operation.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:37:3. After both absence checks succeed, remove the active country's single receipt key. This is the persistent commit point for both version 1 and version 2. A thrown removal leaves the terminal receipt and lock in place. A successful Web Storage removal commits the durable reset. Avoid a further fallible storage read or write between that deletion and clearing memory. There is no secondary receipt key to delete or fall back to.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:38:4. Clear that country's in-memory draft, plan candidate, terms and consent, and attempt and receipt state. Use explicit empty memory state so restoration cannot re-read old objects. Release the in-memory terminal lock last and navigate to canonical same-country Details with fresh configuration and its defaults. Failure to load configuration or complete navigation after the reset uses the wizard's existing recovery paths. It does not revert the reset. Old Summary history entries go through unfinished-quote prerequisites.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:40:If storage cannot be accessed or a required cleanup cannot be verified before the commit point, report a retryable restart failure and stay terminal. A memory-only receipt can restart after the same cleanup succeeds, including when its receipt key was never written. The pre-existing memory fallback still limits reload guarantees when storage was unavailable during approval.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:47:| Store a raw draft and full plan DTO in the receipt | Reformatting would depend on future schemas and expose more editable data to receipt storage. The bounded display snapshot preserves the approved view with less data. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:48:| Add a separate version 2 receipt key or migrate all quote state into one envelope | Both require coordinating old and new keys during restore and reset. Versioning the existing receipt envelope lets one final removal clear either format. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:49:| Clear memory first or delete the receipt before the draft and plan | A failure could reopen a quote with stale data or leave a receipt that returns on reload. The terminal record remains until earlier cleanup is verified. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:53:- **AC-US03-R01** — In CO and CL, verify a completed quote reaches only confirmation through direct URLs, Back, Forward and reload, and edits cannot briefly render. Check legacy receipts and navigation to the other country.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:55:- **AC-US03-R03** — Verify reset of both receipt versions, fresh Details defaults and absence of the old approval after reload and history navigation. Inject failure at each durable cleanup stage, check that reload stays terminal with the existing stored receipt, and verify a retry can complete. Verify no changes to the other country.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:11:[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves a country-scoped terms document and public read action. [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern. [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps quote state and payment in the browser, and [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) already gates editable Summary on valid Details and a freshly revalidated plan. The existing Angular 21.2 wizard has the Summary handoff and the Strapi 5.63 controller already serves Form and Plans through the same-origin proxy. US-03 needs a terms revision contract, a payment attempt that refreshes consent before it starts, and a terminal receipt that survives reload.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:19:Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:37:### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:42:4. Success creates one browser-generated opaque simulated quote number and commits an immutable terminal receipt once. Persist only the minimal completed receipt in a bounded, versioned country-scoped `sessionStorage` record alongside the existing draft and plan entries. Keep country and quote number in the receipt. Decode the record as untrusted input, rejecting oversized, unknown-version, malformed or wrong-country values. Consent and unfinished attempts stay in memory. After reload, an interrupted attempt therefore cannot resume or settle. The person returns through the existing Details and plan checks and can retry after current consent. If storage is unavailable, retain the same duplicate guard and receipt for the current page session under ADR-003. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:43:5. A valid restored receipt is the terminal confirmation for the current country quote. On the Summary route, restore that confirmation without opening editable Summary or presenting live plan, price or terms as part of the receipt. CMS changes and edits reached through browser history cannot alter or reopen a settled result. Switching back to that country preserves the receipt. ADR-003 reserves clearing the country quote for an explicit start-new-quote reset. The current app has no such action, and US-03 requires only the reset boundary. A future explicit reset clears the receipt, draft, plan and in-memory payment state, with the terminal lock cleared last so a partial reset cannot silently reopen the completed quote. Editable Summary for an unfinished or explicitly reset quote still uses the live prerequisite redirects in ADR-004.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:52:| Persist consent and unfinished attempts or require fresh CMS data to restore a receipt | Persisting in-flight state needs restoration rules and risks replay. Revalidating a historical receipt against current editorial data can erase access to a completed result. A minimal terminal record supports reload without reviving unfinished work or copying quote details. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:59:- Use AC-US03-05 through AC-US03-08 and AC-US03-10 / T-US03-05 through T-US03-09 to verify one attempt through both phases, deterministic Approved and Rejected in both countries, retry, late responses after navigation, and reload of interrupted and completed states. Check wrong-country and corrupt storage, memory fallback, and completed receipt recovery after rejected live prerequisites without opening editable Summary. T-US03-10 covers the full flow at project verification.

docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:36:2. Remove the active country's draft and candidate keys and read each back to confirm absence. A failure stops the reset before touching the receipt key. A partially cleared draft or candidate stays inaccessible behind the receipt. Retry repeats the removals safely. The other country is outside this operation.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:37:3. After both absence checks succeed, remove the active country's single receipt key. This is the persistent commit point for both version 1 and version 2. A thrown removal leaves the terminal receipt and lock in place. A successful Web Storage removal commits the durable reset. Avoid a further fallible storage read or write between that deletion and clearing memory. There is no secondary receipt key to delete or fall back to.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:38:4. Clear that country's in-memory draft, plan candidate, terms and consent, and attempt and receipt state. Use explicit empty memory state so restoration cannot re-read old objects. Release the in-memory terminal lock last and navigate to canonical same-country Details with fresh configuration and its defaults. Failure to load configuration or complete navigation after the reset uses the wizard's existing recovery paths. It does not revert the reset. Old Summary history entries go through unfinished-quote prerequisites.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:40:If storage cannot be accessed or a required cleanup cannot be verified before the commit point, report a retryable restart failure and stay terminal. A memory-only receipt can restart after the same cleanup succeeds, including when its receipt key was never written. The pre-existing memory fallback still limits reload guarantees when storage was unavailable during approval.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:47:| Store a raw draft and full plan DTO in the receipt | Reformatting would depend on future schemas and expose more editable data to receipt storage. The bounded display snapshot preserves the approved view with less data. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:48:| Add a separate version 2 receipt key or migrate all quote state into one envelope | Both require coordinating old and new keys during restore and reset. Versioning the existing receipt envelope lets one final removal clear either format. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:49:| Clear memory first or delete the receipt before the draft and plan | A failure could reopen a quote with stale data or leave a receipt that returns on reload. The terminal record remains until earlier cleanup is verified. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:53:- **AC-US03-R01** — In CO and CL, verify a completed quote reaches only confirmation through direct URLs, Back, Forward and reload, and edits cannot briefly render. Check legacy receipts and navigation to the other country.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:55:- **AC-US03-R03** — Verify reset of both receipt versions, fresh Details defaults and absence of the old approval after reload and history navigation. Inject failure at each durable cleanup stage, check that reload stays terminal with the existing stored receipt, and verify a retry can complete. Verify no changes to the other country.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:11:[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves a country-scoped terms document and public read action. [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern. [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps quote state and payment in the browser, and [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) already gates editable Summary on valid Details and a freshly revalidated plan. The existing Angular 21.2 wizard has the Summary handoff and the Strapi 5.63 controller already serves Form and Plans through the same-origin proxy. US-03 needs a terms revision contract, a payment attempt that refreshes consent before it starts, and a terminal receipt that survives reload.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:19:Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:37:### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:42:4. Success creates one browser-generated opaque simulated quote number and commits an immutable terminal receipt once. Persist only the minimal completed receipt in a bounded, versioned country-scoped `sessionStorage` record alongside the existing draft and plan entries. Keep country and quote number in the receipt. Decode the record as untrusted input, rejecting oversized, unknown-version, malformed or wrong-country values. Consent and unfinished attempts stay in memory. After reload, an interrupted attempt therefore cannot resume or settle. The person returns through the existing Details and plan checks and can retry after current consent. If storage is unavailable, retain the same duplicate guard and receipt for the current page session under ADR-003. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:43:5. A valid restored receipt is the terminal confirmation for the current country quote. On the Summary route, restore that confirmation without opening editable Summary or presenting live plan, price or terms as part of the receipt. CMS changes and edits reached through browser history cannot alter or reopen a settled result. Switching back to that country preserves the receipt. ADR-003 reserves clearing the country quote for an explicit start-new-quote reset. The current app has no such action, and US-03 requires only the reset boundary. A future explicit reset clears the receipt, draft, plan and in-memory payment state, with the terminal lock cleared last so a partial reset cannot silently reopen the completed quote. Editable Summary for an unfinished or explicitly reset quote still uses the live prerequisite redirects in ADR-004.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:52:| Persist consent and unfinished attempts or require fresh CMS data to restore a receipt | Persisting in-flight state needs restoration rules and risks replay. Revalidating a historical receipt against current editorial data can erase access to a completed result. A minimal terminal record supports reload without reviving unfinished work or copying quote details. |
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:59:- Use AC-US03-05 through AC-US03-08 and AC-US03-10 / T-US03-05 through T-US03-09 to verify one attempt through both phases, deterministic Approved and Rejected in both countries, retry, late responses after navigation, and reload of interrupted and completed states. Check wrong-country and corrupt storage, memory fallback, and completed receipt recovery after rejected live prerequisites without opening editable Summary. T-US03-10 covers the full flow at project verification.
